chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja' ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Ma'bad, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Khalid, who said: I asked Abul Hassan Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (peace be upon him)

about the Words of Allah, the Exalted, 'We did indeed offer the Trust to the Heavens and the Earth and the Mountains; but they refused to undertake it,' so he said: The Trust is the Mastery. Whoever makes a false claim of Mastery is an unbeliever.

key_terms.الْأَمَانَة: The Trust, interpreted here as spiritual and political authority

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Trust (Amanah) in Surah Al-Ahzab according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (s) identifies the 'Trust' (al-Amanah) of Surah Al-Ahzab as the divine authority of Wilayah, specifically the Imamate. He clarifies that while the heavens and earth refused this heavy burden, the Imams accepted it; consequently, anyone who claims this exclusive spiritual and political authority without legitimate right is deemed an unbeliever (kafir).
